atlases.name: actors
atlases.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
The FIRST reference is the APPROVED visual direction A: premium stylized physically based 3D machinery. Match its convincing modeled armor thickness, generous machined bevels, satin orange enamel and ivory armor, graphite joints, subtly brushed steel and restrained cyan energy glass. Clean continuous surface shading and soft specular reflections, readable large forms, a few corner scuffs. NO black ink outlines, painted brush texture, noisy scratches, flat comic shading or photographic grunge. Preserve the SECOND reference's object identities, palette, slot order and modular design. Change the rendering/material treatment to A. This is production game artwork, not a presentation poster.
Light: broad nearly overhead neutral softbox and gentle fill, shallow consistent local ambient occlusion inside joints; do NOT bake any cast ground shadows or background lighting into the transparent cutouts. Avoid hard directional reflections that become conspicuous when a weapon rotates. Fixed orthographic three-quarter top-down camera, about 35 degrees elevation. Complete crisp silhouettes, fully opaque mechanical bodies and real alpha outside.
Create a portrait production atlas, EXACTLY 4 equal columns and 6 equal rows. Target 1536 x 2304, with 24 separate isolated objects centered in their cells and at least 12% transparent padding on every side. No captions, UI, dividers or floor. Actual alpha background. Do not include any complete assembled hero from reference 1.
Rows 1–4: TORSOS ONLY including shoulders and hip connector, NO LEGS, NO WEAPONS, NO BACKPACK. Each row is the SAME model turned through four directions: column 1 front/down-screen, column 2 right/screen-right, column 3 REAR/up-screen (no face visible), column 4 left/screen-left. Consistent model scale and top-down elevation in all views.
Row 1 scavenger: round ivory torso, two cyan vertical eyes in black glass circular face, orange shoulder shells; use the approved A hero's torso proportions and material.
Row 2 bulwark: wide square heavy armored torso with large orange shoulders and narrow cyan visor.
Row 3 kestrel: slender angular scout torso, two tapered upward orange antenna fins, cyan slit face.
Row 4 hive: round torso, small cylindrical side drone pods and a single cyan face strip.
Row 5: four LEGS-ONLY PAIRS in chassis order scavenger / bulwark / kestrel / hive. Exactly TWO legs per cell, symmetrically spaced about the center, visible hip connector and two complete feet, front/down-screen top-down view. Short sturdy boots; wide heavy boots; thin spring legs; squat curved mechanical legs. No torso or upper body.
Row 6: four BACKPACKS ONLY in matching chassis order: cylindrical cyan-glass energy tank with orange caps and graphite hose; broad rectangular ivory/orange armored battery pack; twin slim vertical cyan thrusters; twin round cyan drone docking ports. No torso or legs.
The second reference shows the correct component identities and row order. Do not copy its illustrated style. Large 3D volume, satin metal and clear surface thickness should remain obvious at small size. Every cell isolated; no touching cells, stray tiny objects, checkerboard, colored background, decorative glow outside silhouettes, text or logos.

Row 2: E07 shield guardian with huge rectangular front shield; E08 red crawler with conical steel drill snout; E09 six-legged cable spider carrying a large cable spool; E10 red cargo crate on crab legs; E11 magnetic ring emitter with circular antennas; E12 heavy sweeper vehicle with broad front roller drum.
Row 3 bosses: B1A huge roller king with giant front drum and two hydraulic arms; B1B tracked magnetic crane with raised boom and hanging round electromagnet; B2A furnace crab with six legs and orange furnace mouth plus two smokestacks; B2B TWO matching magnetic drones side-by-side inside this ONE cell, with an obvious transparent gap between them; B3A towering recycler machine with two crusher arms and circular central red eye; B3B broad orbital carrier craft facing forward with four downward thrusters and separate visible red missile pods at its left and right edges. Keep both carrier side pods clear of the central hull silhouette so each can also be sampled as a detachable module.
Bosses have more visual mass but still fit their cells. Minimal engine emission bounded inside each ship cell. Actual transparent background, no floor, cast shadows, labels, captions, numbers, grid lines, panels, decorative background glow, humans, extra objects or cropped antennas.
atlases.spacingRepairPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
EDIT the supplied transparent enemy atlas for production sprite sampling. Make ONE change: improve CELL SPACING.
Keep all 18 design cells, all exact machine identities, the row/column order, 3D metal rendering, rust-red/graphite colors and orange energy lights unchanged.
The image must remain a 6-column x 3-row landscape grid on actual transparent alpha. Every row is exactly one third of total image height; every column exactly one sixth of width.
SHRINK EACH DESIGN about 20–25 percent relative to its current size, and recenter it within its exact uniform grid cell. Each complete design must fit within the INNER 68% WIDTH AND 68% HEIGHT of its own cell. Leave a completely empty transparent gutter surrounding EVERY cell, at least 12% of cell width/height. In particular, keep all drill tips, crane booms, tripod needles, legs and thruster glows inside their own cells.
No part of any object may enter an adjacent cell. Do not align all objects to the bottom; center each vertically and horizontally in its grid cell.
Row 1: round mite; spike bug; tracked hauler; tall needle tripod; battery bot; repair orb.
Row 2: shield guardian; drill crawler; cable spider; cargo crate crab; magnetic ring emitter; sweeper roller vehicle.
Row 3: roller king; magnetic crane; furnace crab; magnetic twin drones (TWO drones inside this one cell, separated by a transparent gap); prime recycler; orbital carrier with visible left/right missile pods.
Do not redraw a different design, change camera or materials, add ink outlines, recolor, add a background, numbers, text, grid lines, tile borders, cast shadows or extra props. Transparent PNG. This is atlas spacing repair, not a new art direction. Preserve sharp high-quality 3D details.

atlases.name: environment
atlases.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Produce a seamless-looking TOP-DOWN INDUSTRIAL GROUND atlas with EXACTLY 2 columns x 2 rows of equal opaque square tiles, target 1536 x 1536. Reference 1 is the approved A 3D metal material language; reference 2 is the EXISTING ground atlas to upgrade. Keep the same four zones and broad pattern identities but replace painted outlines and noisy scratches with convincing physically based steel surface shading: shallow bevels, subtle recessed seams, soft ambient occlusion in bolt holes, controlled satin roughness. Strict orthographic directly overhead, ZERO perspective tilt.
Top-left: scrapyard floor, low-contrast deep blue-gray broad iron slabs, a few worn joints and bolts.
Top-right: foundry, dark desaturated blue-gray heavy steel panels with sparse recessed vent grates and faint muted copper joints.
Bottom-left: orbital freight dock, dark desaturated navy steel with two narrow recessed parallel cargo tracks and restrained pale gray guide markings.
Bottom-right: neutral maintenance floor, large dark slate iron panels with sparse thin joints.
Every quadrant fills its whole square and aligns exactly at the central vertical/horizontal edges. No frame or gutter. Large mostly calm surfaces, much LESS tiny scratches and noise than reference 2. Readable orange sprites and red hazard zones will appear on top. Keep floor values dark and low contrast, never shiny bright silver. Soft overhead illumination, no vignette, directional long shadows, dramatic highlights, light bloom, tall props, barrels, machines, characters, hazards, text, logo or orange warning stripes. Entire image opaque. Use real 3D material depth within the shallow panel seams while keeping the playable surface visually flat.

atlases.name: cargo
atlases.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a NEW small production transparent sprite atlas containing exactly TWO isolated detachable missile cargo pods, derived from the LEFT AND RIGHT SIDE PODS of the orbital carrier at the BOTTOM RIGHT of reference image 1. Reference image 2 supplies the approved A premium stylized 3D metal rendering.
Horizontal atlas, EXACTLY 2 equal cells in ONE row. Target 1024x512. One complete LEFT carrier pod centered in the left cell; one complete RIGHT carrier pod centered in the right cell. Each object occupies about 65% of its cell dimensions with generous real transparent padding.
These pods are the dark graphite armored rectangular boxes on either side of that carrier. Each has a recessed rust-red rounded-square front panel containing SIX glowing orange circular missile tubes, arranged two columns and three rows. Preserve this exact tube arrangement. Solid thick beveled metal housing, top attachment rail, short side mounting connector; left pod's connector on its RIGHT edge and right pod's connector on its LEFT edge. Show both as independent COMPLETE objects with full finished edges and backs, no cut-off steel, no adjoining central spaceship, no exhaust flames, no wings.
Both look toward the bottom of the screen from the same fixed orthographic three-quarter top-down camera as the carrier, with softly illuminated upper surfaces and visible casing depth. Soft almost-overhead key light and restrained ambient occlusion inside the missile wells. Satin rust-red enamel, dark steel, a few small worn corners. No ink outlines, hand-painted brushwork, dramatic shadow or outside glow.
Actual transparent alpha background, no floor, cast shadow, grid lines, captions, text, number, labels, UI or additional objects. This is a pair of small functional machine-part sprites, not an entire spaceship or a presentation scene.
